<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f7bdefc713dea6c3eeb812e11fd21a0bb16a1efc` — the merge of head `ada9d16be7d93fdf1e297b6483c120840e1d6f0a` into base `e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f7bdefc713dea6c3eeb812e11fd21a0bb16a1efc && git checkout f7bdefc713dea6c3eeb812e11fd21a0bb16a1efc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee ada9d16be7d93fdf1e297b6483c120840e1d6f0a && git checkout -B drift-repro e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee && git merge --no-ff ada9d16be7d93fdf1e297b6483c120840e1d6f0a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `28c3513c7b9e67d210ee320f50b49341d1f830ca`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.disabled-holder-pair-row-bare-read-withheld.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts, .changeset/32814-disabled-holder-pair-row-bare-read.md, .changeset/32814-disabled-holder-pair-row-semantic-entry.md

Face: schema (a `packages/spec/src/**` hit), also declaring a narrowing. Diff read against merge base `199e3624`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `isHoldersPairRow` answers true only for a row stamped with a customization pair (`pairsOf`) of some holder of `(type, name)`, disabled holders included, where the stamp is itself no holder. A holder's own row, a package-less row and a non-pair row all answer false and keep their earlier judgment.
- It is consulted only on the read naming no package that reached an item. The read naming a package keeps its `isStoredUnder` arm, and `object` / `package` keep their own branch. The withholding still requires `disabledOnlyHolderOf`, meaning every holder is disabled, so a pair row beside an enabled holder of the same App is served as before.
- Moved doors: the bare member read, `/layers` (which asks the plain read), and the execution face. List reads are explicitly unchanged.
- Pins: both holder shapes (a module, the App itself) × four save and hydration orders, with a re-enable CONTROL; "withheld equals no row stored"; the two-module CONTROL in both registration orders (one enabled: served; both disabled: withheld); and REST 404 on the plain read and `/layers` in both orders, with a no-row CONTROL. All 67 check runs on this head concluded: 56 success, 11 skipped, none failed.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` (a 200 becomes a 404) with the BREAKING banner and `adr-0087: registered disabled-holder-pair-row-bare-read-withheld`. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is `patch` and `@objectstack/spec` is `patch`.

**Ruling on `Metadata-protocol` (asked by the author): `none` stands.** The line measures what a metadata author can write and what that writing means (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). Here no save is refused and no key or value moves, so it is not `narrowed`. The stored pair row's meaning is also unchanged: it was already the holders' customization, and the pair's own address already withheld it. The move is the bare read door coming into agreement with that, so it is not `semantic` either. Compare #33251, where which package a declared row belongs to changed, so it took `semantic`. #33182's `narrowed` was ruled at its own review and is not re-opened here. The narrowing is carried by `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the BREAKING banner and the registered ADR-0087 entry, which is the right place for it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No governed path. The PR is authored by `objectstack-fleet[bot]` on the relay.
- N1 (nit, residual): the list reads (`getMetaItems`, `getMetaItemsForExecution`) are declared unchanged. If a bare list still serves such a pair row while every holder is disabled, that is the same red line 1 on the list. I recommend measuring it once and filing one loose-ends card if it reproduces. It does not block this PR, which scopes itself honestly.
- N2 (nit, performance): every bare read that reaches a stamped item now runs `packageScopedHoldersOf(…, includeDisabledPackages)` plus `installedManifestsOfEngine` inside `isHoldersPairRow`, before `disabledOnlyHolderOf` is asked. Asking `disabledOnlyHolderOf` first (cheap to answer `undefined` when any holder is enabled, the common case) would skip the pair scan on most reads.
- N3 (nit): a pair row of App A whose disabled holder X shares the name with an enabled holder Y of another App B is not pinned. Reading the code, D3 takes Y's stack, so A's pair row should not be reached. One CONTROL would make that explicit.
- The author's open question (a package-less env row under a disabled-only holder) is out of this diff and goes to the seat for a ruling, as the author proposes.

### ④ Design judgment

`18.disabled-holder-pair-row-bare-read-withheld.ts` holds against ADR-0150 D3 and epic red line 1 (a disabled package is not served). Its `surface` names the three moved doors after the head commit's fix, `replacement` gives a concrete operator action (re-enable a holder), and `acceptanceCriteria` matches the REST pins. The implementing change in `protocol-meta-item-face.ts` agrees with it: the withheld answer is byte-equal to the no-row answer (pinned), so no new response shape leaks. No must-fix or should-fix; N1–N3 are nits. This is the final round.
